1.title: Smart Analytics, Business Intelligence and Streaming
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Smart Analytics, Business Intelligence and Streaming. It covers the exam area two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. two point three Discuss how smart analytics, business intelligence tools and streaming analytics can add value: how Looker democratizes access to data. Analyzing and visualizing Big Query data in Looker. Why real-time streaming analytics is critical. The Google Cloud products that modernize data pipelines (pub sub, Dataflow, Managed Service for Apache Spark). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Exploring data transformation with Google Cloud (about eighteen percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Business intelligence with Looker
1.text: Business intelligence with Looker. Business intelligence (B I) turns data into reports, dashboards and insight that people use to decide. Democratize data. Let many people, not only analysts, answer questions themselves (self-service B I). Semantic layer. Business terms and metrics are defined once so everyone uses the same numbers. Works with Big Query. Live, governed access to the warehouse: real-time reports and dashboards. Embedding and workflows. Put insights inside apps and business processes, not just a report.

1.title: Business intelligence with Looker, continued
1.text: Business intelligence with Looker. The figure shows this: From data sources to Big Query, Looker dashboards and streaming pipelines. Exam tip: Looker equals self-service B I and a single source of truth for metrics. Big Query stores and queries; Looker shows and shares.

1.title: Streaming analytics
1.text: Streaming analytics. Streaming analytics analyzes data as it arrives, not hours later. Process stored data in groups, on a schedule. Process each event within seconds. Good for monthly reports. Good for fraud alerts, live inventory, personalization, monitoring. Why it matters: modern businesses must react now: stop a fraudulent payment, reroute a delivery, adjust a price, personalize a page.

1.title: Products for data pipelines
1.text: Products for data pipelines. pub sub. What it does: Messaging service that ingests and delivers events between systems at scale. Think of it as: The front door for streaming data. Dataflow. What it does: Managed, serverless service for stream and batch processing (Apache Beam). Think of it as: The transformer between source and destination.

1.title: Products for data pipelines, continued
1.text: Products for data pipelines. Managed Service for Apache Spark. What it does: Runs Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs without hand-built clusters (the product earlier named Dataproc). Think of it as: Move existing Spark and Hadoop workloads. Big Query. What it does: Warehouse that also ingests streaming data. Think of it as: The destination for analysis. A typical streaming pipeline: sources to pub sub to Dataflow to Big Query to Looker. Exam tip: pub sub carries the events, Dataflow processes them, Big Query stores them, Looker shows them. Existing Spark or Hadoop jobs to Managed Service for Apache Spark.

1.title: Putting it together
1.text: Putting it together. Business users want live dashboards on the warehouse. Looker on Big Query. Ingest millions of events a second. pub sub. Clean and enrich events in motion. Dataflow. Run an existing Spark job in the cloud. Managed Service for Apache Spark. Exam tip: Real-time words in a question (within seconds, as it happens, live) point to streaming: pub sub plus Dataflow. Self-service words point to Looker.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company wants business users to build their own reports from governed data without asking analysts. Which product fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Looker, a self-service business intelligence platform. Looker democratizes access to data through self-service business intelligence.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A retailer wants dashboards that always use the same definition of revenue. Which Looker feature supports this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A semantic layer that defines metrics once. A semantic layer defines business metrics once so every report uses the same numbers.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A payment company must detect fraud within seconds of each transaction. Which approach fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Real-time streaming analytics on each event. Streaming analytics processes events as they arrive, which fraud detection needs.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which product ingests and delivers millions of events per second between systems? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: pub sub, a messaging service for events. pub sub is the managed messaging service that ingests and delivers events at scale.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which serverless service transforms data in motion, in both streaming and batch jobs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Dataflow, a managed stream and batch processor. Dataflow is the managed service for stream and batch data processing.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company already has Apache Spark jobs and wants to run them in Google Cloud without managing clusters by hand. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Managed Service for Apache Spark. Managed Service for Apache Spark runs existing Spark and Hadoop workloads as a managed service.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does Looker democratize? Answer: Access to data, through self-service business intelligence. Question two. What is pub sub? Answer: A messaging service for events. Question three. What does Dataflow do? Answer: Processes data streams and batches.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which product runs existing Spark jobs? Answer: Managed Service for Apache Spark. Question five. What is streaming analytics? Answer: Analyzing data as it arrives. Question six. Name the streaming pipeline order. Answer: pub sub, Dataflow, Big Query, Looker.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Looker: self-service B I, semantic layer, works on Big Query. Streaming: react in seconds: fraud, inventory, personalization. Pipeline: sources, pub sub, Dataflow, Big Query, Looker. Spark: Managed Service for Apache Spark for existing jobs.
